newsitem.title: USA: BPA offers no power during peak hours Sat or Mon.
newsitem.headline: BPA offers no power during peak hours Sat or Mon.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) continued to refrain from offering power during peak demand hours on Saturday and Monday, but did offer power during the day on Sunday, the agency said Friday.
For Monday, BPA still offered firm power during a block of light-load hours (0100-0600, 2300-2400 PST) at $10.50 per megawatt hour (MWh).

Non-firm power during shoulder hours (1100-1700, 2100-2200 PST) was offered at $11.25 for Northwest deliveries and $12.25 for California-Oregon border (COB) sales, up from a flat price of $10.75 for Friday deliveries.
Non-firm power during off-peak hours on Monday was offered at $10.75 for all deliveries, up from $10.50 for Friday.
BPA offered displacement power during a block from 0100 PST Saturday through 0600 Monday at $6.00 per MWh, compared with $7.00 and $9.00 for off-peak hours on Friday.
